CEAST Melt Flow Series
Product catalog summary
Introduction
The CEAST MF Series Melt Flow Testers are designed to measure the Melt Mass-Flow Rate (MFR) and Melt Volume-Flow Rate (MVR) of thermoplastics, which are critical for characterizing their flow properties. These testers range from simple manual systems to advanced semi-automated systems capable of multi-weight testing.
Importance of Melt Flow Measurement
MFR is a key index for characterizing thermoplastics, providing insights into molecular weight, degradation, and additive quality. It is essential for quality control, ensuring that incoming materials meet specifications and do not disrupt production processes.
Testing Procedures
The document outlines several procedures for melt flow testing:
Procedure A: Mass-measurement method for basic quality control, suitable for MFR ranging from 0.15 – 50 g/10 min.
Procedure B: Volume-measurement method using a piston displacement transducer, suitable for semi-automatic tests.
Procedure C: Modified for fast-flowing materials, requiring a different die geometry.
Procedure D: Multi-weight testing to determine MFR and MVR under different masses, providing Flow Rate Ratio (FRR) data.
Product Range
The CEAST MF Series includes several models:
CEAST MF10: Entry-level model for single-weight tests according to Procedure A.
CEAST MF20: Versatile for single-weight tests with high accuracy and stability.
CEAST MF30: Advanced single-weight tester with features for compacting and purging.
CEAST MF50: Premier model for single and multi-weight tests with high automation and safety features.
Software and Data Management
The VisualMELT Software enhances the functionality of the testers, allowing for:
Control of test procedures and data acquisition.
Editing and storage of test methods.
Real-time graphs and data validation.
Advanced analysis and report management.
Conclusion
The CEAST MF Series Melt Flow Testers provide comprehensive solutions for measuring the flow properties of thermoplastics, essential for quality control, product development, and process optimization in the manufacturing industry.
Overview
The document discusses the features and benefits of CEAST Melt Flow Testers, specifically the MF20, MF30, and MF50 models, highlighting their capabilities in improving safety, efficiency, and compliance with ASTM standards for testing high-flow materials.
Specifications and Features
The CEAST MF20 and MF30 models are equipped with a Manual Mass Selector and an integrated barrel cleaning device. The MF30 also includes a load cell for controlled material compacting and efficient purging. The MF50 model offers advanced features such as an automatic piston holding device and a semi-automatic die plugging device, meeting all ASTM requirements for high-flow materials.
Safety and Efficiency Solutions
The document emphasizes the importance of safety and efficiency in laboratory operations. The CEAST MF50's features, such as the automatic piston holding device and die plugging device, help prevent sample leakage and ensure compliance with ASTM D1238 standards.
Global Support and Quality Assurance
Instron, the manufacturer of CEAST Melt Flow Testers, provides global support with 25 offices in 18 countries. The company operates under ISO 9001 quality standards, ensuring high-quality service, installation, calibration, and technical support.
Technical Specifications
The document provides detailed specifications for each model, including test types, encoder availability, weight lifter options, load cell inclusion, melt cutting device options, test temperature range, temperature accuracy, barrel material, user interface, machine dimensions, and power consumption.
Contact Information
Instron provides contact details for various regions, including the Americas, Europe, Middle East, Africa, Asia, and Australia, ensuring accessibility to support and services worldwide.

Process Optimization
If your laboratory is working with thermoplastic materials, you will need to check the flow properties by comparing values as per standard industrial procedures. The MFR is typically part of the data sheet of a material and can be used to indirectly evaluate other properties. In fact, it’s an index for molecular weight, physical and chemical degradation, and quality of additives and compounds. FRR results indicate qualitative differences for Molecular Weights Distribution and Non-Newtonian Flow Behavior.

Selecting the Right Melt Flow Tester for Your Applications Procedure A (ISO 1133-1/-2*, ASTM D1238) Widely used for basic quality control, this is a mass-measurement method where the operator must weigh portions of the extruded material cut at precise time intervals. The Melt Mass-Flow Rate (MFR) result is directly obtained by dividing the Extrudate Mass by the corresponding Extrusion Time. Standards recommend that this procedure be limited to MFR ranging from 0.15 – 50 g/10 min.
